name: Rebuilt From the Frame
why_it_works: A restoration is a redemption arc in object form: wreck, labor, glory. Swiping slide by slide feels like turning pages of a build log, and the reveal on the last slides rewards the swipe. People share builds because the before shot is so far from the after.

hook.pattern: Slide one shows the wreck at its worst with the price paid or the place it was found.
examples: Found in a field behind a church. Chapter one.
Everybody said scrap it. {{build_hours}} hours later:

slides.headline: Everybody said scrap it
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of a rusted vehicle or worn piece in an overgrown lot, harsh noon sun, wide shot, honest and ugly

slides.headline: Chapter 1: Stripped to nothing
slides.body: Every piece off. Every bolt counted.
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 overhead shot of parts laid out on a garage floor in rows, single shop light, organized chaos

slides.headline: Chapter 2: The worst day
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 close-up of the crack or broken part, dim garage, a single work lamp, grease on the floor

slides.headline: Chapter 3: {{build_hours}} hours
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 photo of hands sanding or welding with sparks, warm orange light, motion blur on sparks

slides.headline: Chapter 4: The detail
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 macro photo of {{finish_detail}} catching light, deep reflections, black background

slides.headline: The reveal
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 hero photo of the finished build at golden hour on a city street, low angle, glossy reflections, {{brand}} plaque visible

slides.headline: Come see it
slides.visual_prompt: 4:5 branded card in {{brand}} colors with the event details in large type

craft.notes: Number the chapters so the swipe feels like reading. Put the lowest point in the middle (chapter 2), not the start, so there is a second dip before the climb. The reveal slide must be the best-lit image in the set.

do_not: Show the finished build on slide one
Use another club's car or plaque
Skip the hard part; the dip is what makes the reveal land
